title: Chinese EV Makers’ European Offensive
gist: Gavekal's AJ Cortese says Chinese EV makers are on track to export over 5mn vehicles in 2026, double 2025, and will next shift production offshore to Europe to get closer to markets and evade tariffs. Half a dozen European projects are under way, often in taken-over plants, so ramp-up may be faster than Japan's in North America; the open question is whether EU regulators can force supply-chain localization and tech transfer. Teaser only.

insights.claim: Chinese EV makers have conquered their home market and are on track to export over 5mn vehicles in 2026, double the 2025 figure.
insights.speaker: AJ Cortese
insights.so_what: Export volume doubling raises pressure on European incumbents and on trade-barrier responses; monitor monthly Chinese export and EU registration data.
insights.quote: Chinese EV makers have conquered their home market and are on track to export over 5mn vehicles this year, double the 2025 figure.

insights.claim: Chinese EV makers' next move is shifting production offshore to be closer to key markets and evade tariffs, with Europe the biggest target.
insights.speaker: AJ Cortese
insights.so_what: Tariffs are pushing a shift from exports to local production, which changes who captures value; watch plant announcements and tariff-exposed European carmakers.

insights.claim: About half a dozen Chinese EV projects are under way in Europe and many more are planned.
insights.speaker: AJ Cortese
insights.so_what: Pipeline of projects signals capacity coming online in the region; track announcements and start-of-production dates.

insights.claim: Chinese EV makers may ramp European production far faster than Japanese carmakers did in North America four decades ago, partly because they are taking over existing plants rather than building new ones.
insights.speaker: AJ Cortese
insights.so_what: Brownfield takeovers shorten time to local output, so competitive pressure on European incumbents may arrive sooner than the Japan analogy suggests.

insights.claim: The key uncertainty is whether EU regulators will succeed in driving localization of supply chains and tech transfer from Chinese EV makers.
insights.speaker: AJ Cortese
insights.so_what: Outcome determines whether Chinese plants in Europe are mere assembly or transfer technology; monitor EU local-content and tech-transfer conditions.
insights.quote: The big question is whether EU regulators will succeed in driving the localization of supply chains and tech transfer.
